notes: Check batch 2026-10-23-check-3: four skill runs (haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), no Opus, so the opus tier is unavailable in per_rule. All have rc 0, head 4215aa3, uncommitted true and skill_hash d31ff0b287f8561f33c3a59ccdbdee00e637c17fc831d4942b2cfad1edf67281, which equals evals/tools/common.py folder_hash of the working tree's idiomatic-elixir/. Each model_id matches its tier; the only other model name in the transcripts is claude-opus-5-5 once per transcript, the tool-definition model option noted in earlier check batches. Each transcript contains the new rule's heading text, so every run read the working-tree SKILL.md. Reads: haiku-1 SKILL.md only (the transcript never contains processes.md text, so Expected reads is missed); the other three SKILL.md, processes.md and ecto-phoenix.md.

Changed rules: git diff d04061d -- idiomatic-elixir/ (working tree) adds one rule, "Break a `->` clause whose pattern and body together pass 70 characters", and changes nothing else. The ten other listed rules are graded to the standard of sweeps/2026-10-23/grades/rate-limiter-skill.json and rate-limiter-baseline.json. The new rule is graded against its text; the sentences that decide the verdicts are "A clause of `case`, `cond`, `with ... else` or `receive` stays on one line while its pattern, the `->` and its body together fit in 70 characters, not counting indentation." and "Once one clause breaks, `mix format` moves every clause's body down and separates the clauses with a blank line; keep that layout, and do not pull the short clauses back onto one line."

New rule, counts: 0 of 4 runs violate it in code; 4 of 4 exercise it (every run has at least one case in code). Every one-line case clause in code was measured after its indentation; none passes 70. The longest are haiku-2 line 150 (64: {:error, reason} -> {:error, {:unreadable_config, path, reason}}), sonnet-1 line 203 (62: {user_id, limit} -> {:error, {:invalid_limit, user_id, limit}}) and sonnet-2 line 203 (60: {:ok, limit} -> {:cont, {:ok, Map.put(parsed, user, limit)}}). Haiku-1 has no one-line clause in code; its only code case (init/1, lines 66-73) is broken. No run has a cond, receive or with ... else. Every case with a broken clause has all its clauses broken with a blank line between them, in code and in doc examples (haiku-1 lines 66-73 and comment lines 149-159; haiku-2 doc lines 35-43; sonnet-1 doc lines 46-55 and code lines 119-137; sonnet-2 doc lines 47-56 and code lines 125-135); no case mixes broken and one-line clauses. One-line fn arguments (sonnet-1 lines 166 and 201, sonnet-2 line 166, haiku-1 lines 98-99) and haiku-2's catch clause at line 158 (51 characters, not one of the four constructs) are outside the rule.

New rule, the one close call: haiku-1 has two over-long clauses outside compiled code, moduledoc line 32 ({:error, {:rate_limited, retry_after_ms}} -> wait_or_reject(retry_after_ms), 75 characters) and line 168 of its commented-out Oban caller ({:error, {:rate_limited, retry_after_ms}} -> {:snooze, div(retry_after_ms + 999, 1000)}, 87 characters). Following 2026-10-23-check-2, which did not count clauses inside @moduledoc examples because layout inside a docstring is not graded and mix format does not touch it, neither is counted, and a comment block is treated the same way. Counting them makes haiku-1 violated and the count 1 of 4. No other run has a doc or comment clause over 70 (the longest is 40).

Standard carried over: an if on one boolean condition, including one joined with and, is clean; a two-step with that calls File.read/1 and JSON.decode/1 directly with no else is clean (haiku-1 lines 107-108, as 2026-10-23-check-2 haiku-2); a two-step with whose body returns a third fallible call is not counted (all four runs); all counts behind GenServer.call violate Pick the abstraction and Use ETS (haiku-1, as 2026-10-23 haiku-1); reading the limits file in init/1 is a missed case check but decides no verdict; key, other, decoded and similar names are not counted under Naming; a comment above a defp that states its effect and gives a reason is clean (haiku-1 lines 92-93, as 2026-10-23 baseline haiku-2 line 154); callers and child lists in @moduledoc count as the run's caller and supervision examples.

Judgment call new to this batch: haiku-1 (line 48) and haiku-2 (line 66) register the process with name: __MODULE__ and accept no :name option, so Write GenServers that stay responsive is violated under "Register singleton processes with `name: __MODULE__`, but let `start_link/1` accept a `:name` option so tests can start their own instance." No earlier rate-limiter run lacked :name, so there is no precedent; the rule text decides it. Haiku-2's two ETS tables also have fixed names (lines 59-60), so a second instance could not start even with a name.

Designs. Haiku-1 keeps every count in one GenServer: check/1 is GenServer.call(__MODULE__, {:check, to_string(user_id)}) and handle_call/3 keeps per-user timestamp lists, with a five-minute sweep. Haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 keep one ETS row per request in a public ordered_set table owned by a GenServer; the caller inserts its row, counts with :ets.select_count/2, and deletes the row when over; a handle_info/2 sweep deletes expired rows. Limits live in a second ETS table (haiku-2) or as rows in the same table (sonnet-1, sonnet-2). Every run reads its JSON limits file inside init/1. Sonnet-1 looks limits up by to_string(user_id) (line 148) but keys counts by the raw id (line 155), so 42 and "42" share a limit but not a count; in a scratch run integer 42 got 5 more after string 42 had used its 5.

Verification, in scratch copies under grader-2026-10-23-check-3-rate-limiter. All four pass mix format --check-formatted and compile with elixirc --warnings-as-errors (Elixir 1.20.3). In every run a 50-task concurrent burst admitted exactly 2 for a user at the default limit of 2 and 5 for user 42, configured at 5. Sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 ran a second instance under name: :other that admitted 2 of 50; haiku-1 and haiku-2 cannot. An injected 61-second-old entry was removed by one sweep message and the live entries kept, in all four.

Violations among the listed rules: haiku-1 three (Pick the abstraction, Use ETS, Write GenServers that stay responsive), haiku-2 one (Write GenServers that stay responsive), sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 none. No rule outside the list was seen broken.
